sections.text: Introduction

This document outline the major maintenance 
procedure P1, which must be performed when the performance of the heat exchanger 
reduce (high pressure drop or insufficient heat transfer)

The heat exchanger function is to transfer heat from 
closed cooling water system to service cooling water system

The first draft initiated and tested by eng. Nasser 
Samra, accepted by general manager eng. Abdel Nasser Abu Taleb, reviewed by MDEPC 
QC eng. Abouda El Bana, approved by eng. Ibrahim Hassan head sector of new Talkha 
P.S and certified by eng. Samir Abdel Gilel MDEPC inspection and quality 
control general director & MPIS coordinator and approved by eng. Mohamed Nageb : 
MDEPC inspection & quality control head sector

Technical Specification of 
the Heat Exchanger

Safety 
Precautions

items:
A work permit must be 
 issued and the qualified maintenance staff should be carry the suitable safety 
 category.

Safety fence 
 with caution marks surrounding the work area is required

Wear your safety helmet, 
 shoes, gloves and glasses
Isolate the heat changer
Cool the heat exchanger

Drain the heat exchanger from the 
 water (both sides : hot & cold)

Make sure the heat exchanger is 
 not under pressure and empty before starting work

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment

items: Complete maintenance tool set

No special tools are required. A 
 ratchet spanner is all that is needed for maintenance and repair (wrench 80)
Cleaning fluid and nylon brushes

sections.text: Work to be carried out
Opening the Heat Exchanger (Figure 2)
Dismantle any connection to the cover
Dismantle the heat exchange movable cover
Clean the thread of the tightening bolts
Apply a thin film of oil to the thread

We advise painting a diagonal line cross the plate 
pack to ensure that the plates are reassembled in the right order
Measure the current A-dimension and record it
Remove bolts (1)

Slacken nuts 2.3, and 4 alternatively so that the 
movable cover can move parallel with the frame plate
Remove bolts 3 and 4
Loosen nuts 2 alternatively

sections.text: Taking Out the Plate

If two or more plates have stuck together, they 
must be separated carefully so that the gaskets are kept on the correct plate

The plates support each other in pairs. If a plate 
ha been so damaged, it must be replaced with an identical one, the adjacent 
plate must also be taken out of the heat exchanger

sections.text: Cleaning the Plates

items: Open the heat exchanger according to a.m.
Steel wool or brushes of carbon steel must not be used

Clean the heat transfer surface of plate in the first step by rinsing 
 with a powerful jet of water and scrubbing with a nylon or similar brush
Take care not to damage the gaskets
Wipe the gaskets dry with a cloth

Inspect carefully the lower portion of each plate as hung in the unit 
 and clean appropriately, as this is the primary area where 
 residual solid material tends to accumulate

Do not use hydrochloric acids, or water containing in excess of (300 ppm) 
 chlorides with stainless steal plates

Limit cleaning solution concentration to 4% strength with temp not exceeding 
 60 C

sections.text: Cleaning the Gasket Groove

items: Clean the plates from residues of old gasket

Small patches of glue that are securely stuck to 
 the gasket groove may remain there they provide an excellent foundation for 
 the new gasket

Wash the gasket groove so that it is completely 
 free of oil and other greasy substances using a rag and acetone or other 
 solvent not containing chlorine compounds
Then let the plate dry off

Glue is applied with a small flat 
brush those parts of the plate's gasket groove in which the gasket lies

Inspect all gasket and surfaces that 
lie against the gasket

The gasket is then placed into 
position on the plate

After drying for about 30 seconds, 
the glue holds the rubber gasket firmly in place in the gasket groove

The plate must then be held under 
light pressure with the aid of other plates or a stiff sheet of other material 
of suitable weight for about half an hour

When the glue joint dried, the gasket 
should be coated with talc to prevent the plates subsequently sticking to each 
other

The plates are then ready to assemble 
into the frame

Plates that have been provided with 
new gaskets must be checked to make sure that the gaskets are in the correct 
gasket groove

Also check the half thickness gaskets 
on the first and last plates

Use the plate sequencing 
specification sheet when started assembly plates to make certain that the plate 
pack is assembled correctly

The plate pack must be compressed to 
a specific thickness - the A- dimension

The A - dimension +/- 3 % gives the 
inside length in millimeters between the fixed and moveable coverA 
 → 0.5 x number of plates = 0.5 
x 320A = 1600 mm 3%
The nuts be tightened alternately

The movable cover plate must be moved parallel to the frame at all times and not 
drawn out of alignment
Tighten bolts (2) alternately
As the resistance increased also tighten bolts 3 and 4 always alternately
Tighten bolts (1)
Check the A - dimension along the heat exchanger
Gasket failure
Possible corrosion in the areas between the ring and diagonal gasket
High pressure or temperature
The compression (A - dimension) is incorrect
Incorrectly positioned or damaged gaskets
A hole / crack in a plate caused by corrosion or mechanical damage
Cracks in the metal liner
The ring gasket on the first plate not sealing correctly to the liner
Foreign particles or other deposit's in the heat exchanger
Deviation in the volumetric flow
Inadequate pump performance
